notes: §1985:VII.4.6.2 prints USE AFTER STANDARD {EXCEPTION | ERROR} PROCEDURE ON {{file-name-1} ... | INPUT | OUTPUT | I-O | EXTEND}, with USE, AFTER, EXCEPTION, ERROR, PROCEDURE and the four mode words underlined and STANDARD and ON not. The superset alternative of useStatement (USE GLOBAL? AFTER? STANDARD? (EXCEPTION | ERROR) PROCEDURE? ON? useOnTarget) parses it, useOnTarget takes exactly one of the four mode words or one or more file-names, and DeclBindUse binds the file list or the open mode as the declarative's scope; the two words 1985 requires and the later format does not are restored at 85 by VisitUseStatement, which refuses a Format 1 USE without AFTER or without PROCEDURE (COBOL0900, use-without-after-2002 and use-without-procedure-2002), and the same member refuses the 2002 formats USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION / EC and EXCEPTION OBJECT (COBOL0877, COBOL0876). Probed at 85: the full spelling with EXCEPTION and with ERROR, STANDARD and ON omitted, two file-names with and without a comma, and each of INPUT, OUTPUT, I-O and EXTEND compile and run (the procedure runs for the files in its scope only); USE without AFTER, without PROCEDURE, without both, with EXCEPTION ERROR together, with BEFORE, with no operand, with no EXCEPTION/ERROR word, with INPUT OUTPUT and with a file-name followed by INPUT are refused. GLOBAL is accepted at 85 because the Inter-Program Communication module prints it (§1985:X.5.5.2). The witness declares USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE ON F1 and shows the procedure run on an at end READ with no AT END phrase (USE 10).

next.reason: 1985: "USE AFTER STANDARD {EXCEPTION|ERROR} PROCEDURE ON (AFTER, PROCEDURE underlined)"; 2023: "USE [ GLOBAL ] AFTER STANDARD ... PROCEDURE ON; AFTER and PROCEDURE printed without underlining". Same structure, but 2023 adds an optional GLOBAL phrase absent from the 1985 format. AFTER and PROCEDURE, required words in 1985, are not underlined in 2023, so programs may omit them.
